# Dashboard

The dashboard is your home in Aevum — the page you land on when you sign in. It's a
single glance that answers the questions you actually open a finance app to ask, without
making you dig through it: **where do I stand, what needs me, how am I trending, and
what's coming up.**

Nothing here is a dead end. Every part of the page is a summary of a fuller feature, and
each one links straight through to it — so the dashboard is a starting point, not a place
you get stuck.

## The top of the page

The headline greets you and shows the week you're in, then leads with the number that
matters most to how you use Aevum:

- If you're using Aevum as a self-tax tool, you'll see how much you've set aside this
  week beside how much you've actually saved toward it.
- If you've turned the tax off and are using Aevum as a plain expense tracker, the same
  spot leads with this month's spending and how much budget room you have left.

Either way it's a live number — it moves as you spend, so you're never waiting until the
end of the week or month to find out where you landed.

## What needs your attention

Just below, Aevum surfaces anything that genuinely needs you — a bill that's overdue, a
budget you've gone over, or a setup step you haven't finished — in one short, prioritized
list with the most pressing thing on top.

When there's nothing to act on, this space simply isn't there. Aevum won't invent a chore
to fill it, so seeing nothing means you're clear.

If you're new, this is also where Aevum keeps a gentle "finish setting up" prompt until
you've added your first account and imported some activity.

## How you're trending

Next is the picture of your spending over time — your recent weeks at a glance, where the
money went by category, and which categories are running hot against their budgets. It's
the "am I on track" view, meant to be read in a couple of seconds rather than studied.

## Recent and upcoming

At the bottom sit two companions: the transactions you've logged most recently, and the
bills coming due in the next week. Together they close the loop from what just happened to
what's about to — and each links out to the full history or the full schedule when you
want more than the next few days.

## A page that moves with you

The dashboard animates gently as it loads — cards ease in, and the key figures count up to
their values — so it feels calm rather than busy. If you prefer things still, turning on
reduced motion (in Aevum or in your device settings) stops all of it, and every number is
already correct the moment the page appears.
